$comment: Pre-existing operator actions with no reachable audit write (lint:audit-log).
This list may only SHRINK. Adding an entry means accepting a mutating
operator action whose occurrence leaves no trace — fix it or write a
`// @no-audit-required: <reason>` comment above the export instead.
MEASURED 2026-08-16, first run: 88 "use server" modules scanned, 37
operator+mutating actions derived, 25 already reach an audit write. These
12 are DEBT, not a verdict — each still owes a decision, and the three
shapes they fall into are NOT equally defensible:
· case-operator (addCaseNote/closeCase) — the fact lands in the
append-only case_events spine, which carries its own actor. Arguably
covered by a different ledger; needs a PO call on whether the
accountability query is expected to find it in audit_log.
· admin-proposals, service-offerings, revocation-evidence — the mutated
row itself records who acted (approval_requests, offerings), so the
trail exists but is not queryable alongside every other operator act.
· alert-subscriptions, novedades, outbox retry — operator preferences,
a read watermark, and a delivery retry. The weakest case for an audit
row, and the best candidates for an explicit @no-audit-required.
SECOND MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-22 — the fence's aperture changed, not the code.
Until this date OPERATOR_GUARDS held only the four admin/govt guards, so
EVERY capability-gated org write was structurally invisible: not baselined,
not exempted, never derived as a candidate at all. The fence's summary line
said "coverage clean" about a set that excluded the whole class — which is
how the org bite report (a legally consequential status imposed on a third
party's animal, top-10 review H1) went a year with no audit row and nothing
noticed. Adding `requireCapability` + `requireCapabilityForOrgToken` made 20
actions visible for the first time. Triage:
· 3 are READS the one-hop heuristic reached through a repository whose
OTHER methods write (checkAdopterAccount, searchFosterVolunteers,
validateIntakeCsv). The rule is about mutations, so they carry an
@no-audit-required in source, next to the code, not an entry here.
· 17 are added below. They are NOT new offences — they offended all along
and could not be seen. Two shapes, matching the two open questions above:
pet_events-backed (attendance-attended, chip-match, intake x2,
org note, adoption info-requested): the fact lands in the append-only
spine with recorded_by_user_id AND author_organization_id. Same
argument as case-operator, and it is deliberately NOT resolved here —
"does the accountability query expect to find this in audit_log?" is
a PO call, and answering it with an @no-audit-required would settle it
by fiat in a commit about a fence.
row-records-the-actor (attendance no-show/cancel, schedule rules x3,
service offerings x5, foster proposal cancel): the mutated row carries
who and when, but the act is not queryable alongside every other
operator act. Same shape as the service-offerings entries already
above, which is why they join them rather than getting an exemption.
Regenerate with: pnpm tsx scripts/check-audit-log-coverage.ts --write-baseline
(only ever to SHRINK the list — the fence fails on a stale entry, so a
fixed action must be removed here in the same commit that fixes it.
NOTE: --write-baseline rewrites this $comment with its own four fixed lines,
so everything above would be lost. Edit the `unaudited` array by hand.)
THIRD MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-17 — and the first time entries LEAVE.
The case-operator pair (addCaseNote/closeCase) is gone from the list below
because both now write an audit row, joined by a third that shipped audited
(escalateCase, the last piece of #41). That answers the open question the
2026-08-16 note left for the PO — does the accountability query expect to
find a case-file act in audit_log? — and it answers YES.
THE ARGUMENT, since a later reader will want it: the cost is asymmetric. A
redundant row harms nobody. A Ley 25.326 query that does NOT find that an
identified authority closed a legal case file does, and the absence of that
row is permanently indistinguishable from the absence of the act it would
have described. The spine keeps recording the ASSERTION; the audit row
records the ADMINISTRATIVE ACT with its before/after status. Same argument
the professional rabies close wrote on 2026-08-17, applied to its neighbour.
WHAT FORCED IT — a fence defect, not a plan, and worth knowing: the
escalation needed writeAuditLog imported into operator-actions.ts, and this
fence measures coverage over the action body PLUS the modules it calls into
one hop, at MODULE granularity. The import alone made the fence declare both
baselined actions covered while neither wrote a row — a FALSE POSITIVE, the
mirror of the one-hop false negative the script header already documents.
Deleting the two entries to satisfy the fence would have recorded that
falsehood permanently. Making them true was the only honest way out.
NOT RESOLVED HERE: the six pet_events-backed entries from the 2026-08-22
measurement share the shape but not the act. A note or a close on a CASE
FILE is an authority act on a legal record; an attendance mark or an intake
is a clinical or operational fact. The precedent now exists, and each of
those six still owes its own decision — settling them by citing this one
would be the fiat this file already refused once.
